description: Soy Mica, estudiante de Electrónica Industrial y Automática. Me gusta crear proyectos y aprender juntos. Quiero contar las historias de los equipos que la NASA dejó en la Luna y Marte mediante una experiencia visual e interactiva. Busco compañeros con interés en programación, diseño, narración o ciencia. No hace falta saber de todo: cada persona puede aportar sus habilidades, aprender con el equipo y ayudarnos a crear un proyecto que acerque la exploración espacial a todo el mundo.
summary:
"Echoes of Space" is a 47 page illustrated mystery book for children aged 8 to 11. It follows three young characters, Vera, Nora and Leo, as they investigate a mysterious piece of equipment that seems to send signals without electricity. Their search takes them across the Moon, Mars and deep space, where they uncover the stories behind eight real pieces of NASA technology.

Through the mystery, readers discover how NASA engineers and scientists use lunar exploration vehicles, Mars instruments, ice detecting tools, seismometers, helicopter rotors and communication antennas to explore space. By combining storytelling, humor and real science, the book makes complex space technology easier and more exciting for young readers to understand.

Alongside the book, we also used AI tools to help create an interactive game based on its story and scientific discoveries. The game is included in our project Google Drive folder as an HTML file that can be downloaded and opened directly in a web browser.

Our goal is to encourage curiosity about space and show children that science and engineering are about creativity, exploration and solving problems.
details:
Echoes of Space: The Mystery of the Impossible Signal is a 47 page digital book designed for children aged 8 to 11 and anyone curious about space. It combines an illustrated mystery with real NASA technology and discoveries. The story follows three friends preparing a museum exhibition who come across an equipment label describing something that can return signals without electricity. Their investigation takes them through eight examples of NASA technology, eventually leading them to discover the answer.

Each piece of equipment plays a role in the mystery while introducing readers to real space exploration. They discover how the Apollo 15 lunar rover helped astronauts explore the Moon, how Mars rovers study rocks, how NASA investigates underground ice and planetary activity, and how Ingenuity achieved powered flight on Mars. The story also introduces Voyager 1 and the technology that allows it to communicate with Earth. The mystery is solved when the characters discover Apollo 15's laser retroreflector, which reflects laser light sent from Earth without needing electrical power.

The main benefit of the project is that it makes real science easier to understand without turning the experience into a traditional lesson. Instead of simply presenting facts, the book lets readers discover scientific ideas alongside the characters. It also highlights why older missions and equipment remain important, showing that even technology left on the Moon or data collected by past missions can continue to contribute to science today.

Alongside the book, we also developed an interactive game based on its story and scientific content. We used AI tools to help create the game, turning some of the book's ideas and discoveries into a more hands-on experience. This gives readers another way to engage with the project and test what they have learned. The game is included in our Google Drive project folder as an HTML file, which can be downloaded and opened directly in any compatible web browser.

We wanted to create something that encourages curiosity, critical thinking and an interest in science and engineering. The book also helps readers understand the difference between scientific evidence and assumptions. For example, it explains that evidence of ancient water does not automatically mean life was found on Mars, and that reflecting a laser is not the same as generating a new signal.

The project was developed as a digital PDF book using writing and document-editing software to create, organize and refine the story, as well as design and arrange the pages and illustrations. AI tools were also used to assist in developing the accompanying interactive game. We focused on making both experiences easy to access and engaging for the intended audience. We also produced a separate 28-second video introducing the project and showing actual pages from the book.

Creativity was central to our approach. Rather than making a collection of unrelated facts about NASA, we connected eight real technologies through one continuous fictional mystery and expanded the experience with an interactive game. The characters, museum and investigation are fictional, but the science and engineering are based on NASA's original sources. We also paid attention to scientific accuracy, image credits, accessibility and the distinction between authentic photographs, enhanced images and historical artist concepts.

Our intended impact is to make children more interested in space exploration and help them see science as a process of asking questions, investigating evidence and discovering unexpected answers. We hope readers finish the project not only knowing more about NASA technology, but also wanting to learn more about the universe.
